answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small, time-vested stake before it may trade — an ember of commitment that must stay lit to earn trust. Reputation then accrues only through verified work, so a flood of fake identities faces a canyon of cost: each clone must fund its own stake and wait out the same aging period. Attackers can mint a thousand names, but they cannot fake the horizon of history — the long, checkable trail of honest transactions that real agents accumulate and cheap copies lack.
